Under the current grant offer letter, the final payment is linked to the final assessment taking place, regardless of whether the NQSW has met the standard.

Do not issue an ASYE completion certificate where the outcome is fail.

Deadline

10 March 2027.

Category 6: NQSWs whose ASYE is deferred

Claim route

Advance claim for the final £1,000 where the NQSW has not reached final assessment because their ASYE is deferred.

What the employer must provide or do

provide the deferral reason and expected completion date, where known

include the participant in the updated application spreadsheet and consolidated Annex D

continue supporting and assessing the participant through to completion

An advance payment does not represent completion. Do not issue an ASYE completion certificate until the NQSW completes successfully.

Deadline

10 March 2027.

How to submit a normal completion claim

Employers should complete the following steps when submitting a normal completion claim.

Step 1: Check eligibility and previous payments

Employers should check that:

the NQSW was registered with DfE

the NQSW was eligible for grant funding

the registration payment has been claimed or recorded

the final £1,000 has not already been paid

the participant’s Social Work England registration details are accurate

Step 2: Complete the claim documents

Employers should submit:

a completed and signed Annex C: Grant Claim Form for Funding in Arrears

the ASYE application spreadsheet updated with the participant’s details included in the claims

a completed and signed ASYE Completion Declaration and Funding Return covering all completion claims included in that funding window

any other supporting document expressly required under the grant offer letter

Participant details should match those supplied in the original ASYE application spreadsheet.

Employers must submit an Annex C with each claim for registration or completion funding made in arrears.

Where an employer submits registration and completion claims together during the same payment window, the Annex C should cover the total amount being claimed for that period and reconcile with the accompanying application spreadsheet.

Step 3: Complete the employer assurance

The Completion Declaration and Funding Return asks employers to confirm that:

ASYE was delivered and assessed against the national framework

a final assessment decision was reached through the employer’s moderation or quality assurance process

the required evidence is held in the employer’s portfolio

mapping against the relevant professional standards is complete

local requirements and Social Work England registration have been checked

a completion certificate has been issued where the participant completes successfully

evidence will be retained and provided if requested for audit or assurance

The form must be authorised by the:

ASYE coordinator or manager

finance approver

a director or delegated senior officer

Step 4: Submit the claim

Email the completed documents to: CFASYE.payments@education.gov.uk.

Use the subject line: ASYE March 2027 final claim: [enter employer name]

Do not send participant portfolios or detailed practice evidence unless DfE requests them. Employers should retain this evidence for audit and assurance purposes.

How to claim for an NQSW completing after 10 March 2027

For each participant who will not complete by 10 March 2027, employers should:

confirm that the NQSW remains on the employer’s ASYE programme

confirm that the final £1,000 has not previously been paid

provide the original registration details

provide the expected completion date, where known

explain whether the participant has an extension or deferral

complete and sign Annex D: Grant claims in advance, which is contained within the Grant Offer Letter (one consolidated Annex D per employer)

include the participant in the updated ASYE application spreadsheet

submit the advance claim by the final deadline of 10 March 2027

Advance payment does not mean that the participant has completed ASYE. The employer must continue to:

provide appropriate supervision and development support

assess the participant against the applicable ASYE framework and professional standards

complete its moderation or quality assurance process

record the final outcome

issue the employer’s ASYE completion certificate where the participant completes successfully

retain the evidence required under the grant agreement

Published guidance makes clear that employers are responsible for completing ASYE for deferred participants and others who continue beyond March 2027.

Activity requirements after the final claims deadline 10 March 2027

After the final claims deadline:

employers must continue supporting participants for whom they have received an advance final payment

employers remain responsible for the final assessment and completion decision

no further ASYE completion payment will be due for a participant whose final £1,000 has been paid in advance

employers must keep appropriate participant, assessment, moderation and grant records

DfE may request evidence for grant assurance or audit

ASYE certificates

The employer is responsible for assuring successful completion and issuing the NQSW’s ASYE certificate.

DfE can provide a separate certificate template on request. To request a copy, contact CFASYE.queries@education.gov.uk.

The template is not part of the grant offer letter.

Employers should not issue a completion certificate solely because an advance payment has been received.

A certificate should only be issued following successful completion of the employer’s assessment and quality assurance process.

Records and assurance

Employers must retain evidence required by the grant agreement and provide it if requested by DfE for assurance or audit.

Employers must retain sufficient evidence to demonstrate that:

the participant was eligible for funding
